examples.english: The surgery was postponed because of adverse weather conditions.
examples.persian: عمل جراحی به دلیل شرایط جوی نامطلوب به تعویق افتاد.

examples.english: The new medication can cause adverse effects in some patients.
examples.persian: این داروی جدید می‌تواند در برخی بیماران عوارض نامطلوبی ایجاد کند.

examples.english: Farmers struggled with an adverse combination of drought and frost this year.
examples.persian: کشاورزان امسال با ترکیبی نامطلوب از خشکسالی و یخبندان دست‌وپنجه نرم کردند.

miniContext: Weather forecasters, doctors, and economists all rely on the word “adverse” to warn people before something works against their interests. A storm can create adverse driving conditions, just as a new medication can trigger adverse reactions in a patient's body. Investors also speak of adverse market movements when prices turn against their expectations. In every case, something described as adverse is actively unfavorable, not simply absent of benefit.

examples.english: The coach encouraged the players to adopt a more aggressive style in the second half.
examples.persian: مربی از بازیکنان خواست در نیمه دوم سبک تهاجمی‌تری در پیش بگیرند.

examples.english: Doctors recommended an aggressive course of treatment to stop the tumor from spreading.
examples.persian: پزشکان یک دوره درمان تهاجمی را برای متوقف کردن گسترش تومور توصیه کردند.

examples.english: The company's aggressive expansion into foreign markets alarmed its competitors.
examples.persian: گسترش تهاجمی شرکت به بازارهای خارجی رقبایش را نگران کرد.

miniContext: Aggressive behavior involves unusual force or intensity, whether in sport, medicine, or business. A boxer might fight aggressively to control a match, while a doctor might choose an aggressive treatment to fight a fast-growing disease. Companies, too, can pursue aggressive strategies, expanding quickly into new markets regardless of the risk. The common thread is a willingness to push hard rather than wait passively for results.

examples.english: The report revealed an alarming rise in ocean temperatures over the past decade.
examples.persian: این گزارش افزایش نگران‌کننده‌ای در دمای اقیانوس‌ها طی دهه گذشته را نشان داد.

examples.english: Doctors noticed an alarming change in the patient's heart rate during the night.
examples.persian: پزشکان در طول شب تغییری نگران‌کننده در ضربان قلب بیمار مشاهده کردند.

examples.english: Deforestation is continuing at an alarming pace in the Amazon basin.
examples.persian: جنگل‌زدایی در حوضه آمازون با سرعتی نگران‌کننده ادامه دارد.

miniContext: News reports often use alarming to describe statistics or trends serious enough to cause real concern. A sudden alarming rise in a disease's spread, for instance, can prompt governments to act quickly. Doctors use the same word when a patient's vital signs change in a way that demands urgent attention. Unlike milder words such as surprising, alarming signals that the situation may require an immediate response.

examples.english: The novel's arrogant protagonist refuses to admit he is ever wrong.
examples.persian: قهرمان متکبر این رمان حاضر نیست هیچ‌وقت اشتباه خودش را بپذیرد.

examples.english: Her arrogant tone during the interview cost her the job offer.
examples.persian: لحن متکبرانه او در مصاحبه باعث شد پیشنهاد شغلی را از دست بدهد.

examples.english: Even his greatest admirers found his arrogant dismissal of criticism hard to forgive.
examples.persian: حتی بزرگ‌ترین ستایشگرانش هم رد متکبرانه او نسبت به انتقادها را سخت می‌بخشیدند.

miniContext: An arrogant person believes their own opinions and abilities are superior to everyone else's, often to the point of dismissing other people's views without consideration. This trait appears frequently in literature, where arrogant characters learn hard lessons about humility. In everyday life, arrogant behavior at work can damage relationships even when the person's skills are genuinely impressive. The word carries a clearly negative judgment, unlike confident, which can be a compliment.

examples.english: There was an awkward silence after he mentioned her ex-husband by mistake.
examples.persian: بعد از اینکه او به اشتباه از همسر سابقش نام برد، سکوتی معذب‌کننده حاکم شد.

examples.english: The new intern felt awkward standing alone at the office party.
examples.persian: کارآموز جدید در جشن اداره، تنها ایستاده بود و احساس معذب بودن می‌کرد.

examples.english: He made an awkward attempt to dance, tripping over his own feet.
examples.persian: او تلاش ناشیانه‌ای برای رقصیدن کرد و پایش به خودش گیر کرد.

miniContext: Awkward describes moments, movements, or feelings that lack grace or ease, from a clumsy physical motion to an uncomfortable silence at a dinner table. A new employee might feel awkward at their first office party, unsure how to join the conversation. The word also applies to physical actions, like an awkward attempt to dance or carry too many bags at once. Whether social or physical, awkward situations usually resolve once familiarity grows.

examples.english: Critics accused the newspaper of running a biased account of the election.
examples.persian: منتقدان روزنامه را به ارائه گزارشی جانبدارانه از انتخابات متهم کردند.

examples.english: The judge was removed from the case for being biased toward one party.
examples.persian: قاضی به دلیل جانبداری از یکی از طرفین از پرونده کنار گذاشته شد.

examples.english: A small, biased sample can make a scientific survey's results meaningless.
examples.persian: یک نمونه کوچک و جانبدارانه می‌تواند نتایج یک پژوهش علمی را بی‌اعتبار کند.

miniContext: A biased account, judge, or sample favors one side unfairly instead of treating all sides equally. Journalists accused of biased reporting are seen as abandoning the neutrality their profession requires. In science, a biased sample can quietly distort an entire study's conclusions, even when the researchers have good intentions. Recognizing bias, whether in media, law, or research, is essential to evaluating information critically.

examples.english: Her blunt feedback stung at first, but it helped him improve his writing.
examples.persian: بازخورد صریح و بی‌پرده او در ابتدا آزاردهنده بود، اما به او کمک کرد نوشتنش را بهتر کند.

examples.english: The editor gave a blunt assessment of the manuscript's weaknesses.
examples.persian: ویراستار ارزیابی صریح و بی‌پرده‌ای از نقاط ضعف دست‌نوشته ارائه کرد.

examples.english: He has always been blunt about his opinions, even when they upset people.
examples.persian: او همیشه درباره نظراتش صریح و بی‌پرده بوده است، حتی وقتی باعث ناراحتی دیگران می‌شود.

miniContext: Blunt speech says exactly what the speaker thinks, without softening the message to protect anyone's feelings. An editor giving blunt feedback on a manuscript might point directly to its weaknesses rather than offering vague praise. People who are blunt are often respected for their honesty, even when their directness stings at first. The word can describe both a person's general manner and a single blunt remark.

examples.english: Employees are allowed to wear casual clothes on Fridays.
examples.persian: کارمندان اجازه دارند روزهای جمعه لباس غیررسمی بپوشند.

examples.english: Their conversation drifted from business matters to more casual topics like travel.
examples.persian: گفتگوی آن‌ها از مسائل کاری به موضوعات غیررسمی‌تری مثل سفر کشیده شد.

examples.english: He mentioned the promotion in such a casual way that no one realized its importance.
examples.persian: او ارتقای شغلی‌اش را به شکلی آنچنان غیررسمی مطرح کرد که هیچ‌کس به اهمیتش پی نبرد.

miniContext: Casual describes anything relaxed or informal, from the clothes people wear on a Friday to the tone of an unplanned conversation. Many offices now allow casual dress to make employees feel more comfortable. A casual remark, meanwhile, lacks the seriousness or weight of something official. The opposite of casual is usually formal, which implies more structure and higher stakes.

examples.english: The theater agreed to accommodate wheelchair users by adding a ramp at the entrance.
examples.persian: سالن تئاتر پذیرفت که با افزودن یک سطح شیب‌دار در ورودی، شرایط را برای استفاده‌کنندگان از ویلچر فراهم کند.

examples.english: Good managers try to accommodate their employees' different working styles.
examples.persian: مدیران خوب سعی می‌کنند سبک‌های کاری متفاوت کارمندان خود را در نظر بگیرند.

examples.english: The hotel could not accommodate such a large group on such short notice.
examples.persian: هتل نتوانست چنین گروه بزرگی را با این اطلاع کوتاه مدت جای دهد.

miniContext: To accommodate someone means to adjust your plans, space, or behavior to meet their needs. A hotel might struggle to accommodate an unusually large group that arrives without notice, while a thoughtful manager tries to accommodate employees who have different working styles. The word also describes physical capacity, as when a building is designed to accommodate wheelchair users. At its core, accommodate is about making room for something or someone else.

examples.english: The smartphone market has become extremely competitive in the last five years.
examples.persian: بازار گوشی‌های هوشمند در پنج سال گذشته بسیار رقابتی شده است.

examples.english: She has always had a competitive streak, even in casual board games.
examples.persian: او همیشه حس رقابتی قوی داشته، حتی در بازی‌های رومیزی معمولی.

examples.english: To win the contract, the firm had to offer a more competitive price.
examples.persian: برای بردن قرارداد، شرکت مجبور شد قیمتی رقابتی‌تر ارائه دهد.

miniContext: A competitive market, person, or price involves active rivalry, where success depends on outperforming others. The smartphone industry, for example, has become intensely competitive as companies race to release new features first. A competitive person may show the same drive even in casual games with friends. In business, offering a competitive price often determines whether a company wins or loses a contract.

examples.english: Analysts gave a conservative estimate of next year's economic growth.
examples.persian: تحلیلگران برآوردی محتاطانه از رشد اقتصادی سال آینده ارائه دادند.

examples.english: Her grandparents held fairly conservative views on marriage and family life.
examples.persian: پدربزرگ و مادربزرگش دیدگاه‌های نسبتاً محافظه‌کارانه‌ای درباره ازدواج و زندگی خانوادگی داشتند.

examples.english: The investor chose a conservative portfolio to protect his savings from market swings.
examples.persian: سرمایه‌گذار یک سبد محتاطانه برای محافظت از پس‌اندازش در برابر نوسانات بازار انتخاب کرد.

miniContext: Conservative describes caution and resistance to sudden change, whether applied to politics, financial estimates, or personal style. A conservative estimate of economic growth assumes the safest, least optimistic outcome rather than the most hopeful one. In social contexts, conservative values tend to favor tradition over rapid change. Investors with a conservative strategy prioritize protecting their money over chasing high but risky returns.

examples.english: Clean water access is critical to public health in refugee camps.
examples.persian: دسترسی به آب تمیز برای سلامت عمومی در اردوگاه‌های پناهجویان بسیار حیاتی است.

examples.english: The critics were highly critical of the film's slow pacing.
examples.persian: منتقدان نسبت به ریتم کند فیلم بسیار انتقادی بودند.

examples.english: The next few hours will be critical in deciding whether the patient recovers.
examples.persian: چند ساعت آینده در تعیین اینکه آیا بیمار بهبود می‌یابد یا نه، بسیار حیاتی خواهد بود.

miniContext: Critical has two related but distinct uses: something essential to an outcome, and someone who judges harshly. Clean water access is critical to survival in a refugee camp, meaning it cannot be missed. A film critic, meanwhile, might be highly critical of a movie's pacing, pointing out its flaws in detail. Context usually makes clear which sense is meant, though both share a sense of close, serious attention.

examples.english: The team switched to a defensive strategy to protect their narrow lead.
examples.persian: تیم برای حفظ برتری اندک خود به استراتژی تدافعی روی آورد.

examples.english: He became defensive as soon as his work was questioned.
examples.persian: به محض اینکه کارش زیر سوال رفت، حالت تدافعی گرفت.

examples.english: The castle's thick walls were part of its ancient defensive design.
examples.persian: دیوارهای ضخیم قلعه بخشی از طرح تدافعی باستانی آن بودند.

miniContext: Defensive describes behavior or design meant to protect against attack, whether on a sports field, in a conversation, or around a castle. A team losing a narrow lead often shifts to a defensive strategy to prevent the other side from scoring. People can also become defensive emotionally, reacting sharply when their work or decisions are questioned. The word always implies guarding against a perceived threat.

examples.english: The teacher asked the disruptive student to leave the classroom.
examples.persian: معلم از دانش‌آموز مختل‌کننده خواست کلاس را ترک کند.

examples.english: Streaming services had a disruptive effect on the traditional television industry.
examples.persian: سرویس‌های پخش آنلاین تأثیر مختل‌کننده‌ای بر صنعت تلویزیون سنتی داشتند.

examples.english: Construction noise next door has been disruptive to the whole neighborhood.
examples.persian: سر و صدای ساخت‌وساز در همسایگی برای کل محله مختل‌کننده بوده است.

miniContext: Disruptive describes something that interrupts or interferes with normal order, whether in a classroom, an industry, or a neighborhood. A disruptive student might be asked to leave class so others can keep learning. In business, disruptive technology can upend an entire industry, as streaming did to traditional television. The word carries a sense of unwelcome interruption, even when the disruption eventually leads to improvement.

examples.english: Wolves are the dominant predator in this forest ecosystem.
examples.persian: گرگ‌ها شکارچی غالب در این اکوسیستم جنگلی هستند.

examples.english: English remains the dominant language of international business.
examples.persian: زبان انگلیسی همچنان زبان غالب تجارت بین‌المللی است.

examples.english: Brown eyes are usually produced by a dominant gene.
examples.persian: رنگ چشم قهوه‌ای معمولاً توسط یک ژن غالب ایجاد می‌شود.

miniContext: Dominant describes whatever holds the most power, influence, or presence in a given situation. In nature, a dominant predator controls access to food and territory within its ecosystem. In genetics, a dominant gene is the one whose trait appears even when only one copy is inherited. The word also applies to languages, cultures, or companies that overshadow their rivals in reach and influence.

examples.english: The city has seen a dramatic increase in tourism since the new airport opened.
examples.persian: این شهر از زمان افتتاح فرودگاه جدید، افزایش چشمگیری در گردشگری داشته است.

examples.english: She made a dramatic entrance at the gala, dressed in bright red.
examples.persian: او با لباسی قرمز پررنگ، ورودی چشمگیری به جشن داشت.

examples.english: The negotiations ended with a dramatic last-minute agreement.
examples.persian: مذاکرات با یک توافق چشمگیر و لحظه آخری به پایان رسید.

miniContext: Dramatic describes change or behavior so sudden or striking that it demands attention. A dramatic increase in tourism can transform a city's economy within a few years. The word also describes theatrical gestures, like a dramatic entrance at a party, or unexpected turns of events, such as a dramatic last-minute agreement in negotiations. In every case, dramatic implies a noticeable departure from the ordinary.

examples.english: The soldier's emotional reunion with his family was broadcast on the evening news.
examples.persian: دیدار احساسی سرباز با خانواده‌اش در اخبار شامگاهی پخش شد.

examples.english: Grief counselors help people cope with the emotional impact of losing a loved one.
examples.persian: مشاوران سوگ به افراد کمک می‌کنند با تأثیر احساسی از دست دادن عزیزانشان کنار بیایند.

examples.english: Buying a house is often an emotional decision as much as a financial one.
examples.persian: خرید خانه اغلب به همان اندازه که یک تصمیم مالی است، تصمیمی احساسی نیز هست.

miniContext: Emotional describes anything connected to feeling rather than pure logic or calculation. An emotional reunion between family members often moves everyone who witnesses it, while an emotional decision, like buying a house, blends feeling with practical judgment. Counselors who help people manage grief are essentially guiding them through the emotional impact of loss. The word highlights the role feelings play even in situations that seem mostly practical.

examples.english: The landlord was fined for charging excessive fees to his tenants.
examples.persian: صاحب‌خانه به دلیل دریافت هزینه‌های بیش از حد از مستأجرانش جریمه شد.

examples.english: Excessive rainfall caused the river to overflow its banks.
examples.persian: باران بیش از حد باعث شد رودخانه از کرانه‌هایش طغیان کند.

examples.english: Doctors warned that excessive use of painkillers can damage the liver.
examples.persian: پزشکان هشدار دادند که مصرف بیش از حد داروهای ضددرد می‌تواند به کبد آسیب برساند.

miniContext: Excessive describes an amount or degree that goes well beyond what is reasonable or necessary. A landlord charging excessive fees is demanding more than is fair, just as excessive rainfall can overwhelm a river's banks. Doctors warn against the excessive use of painkillers because even helpful medicine becomes harmful past a certain point. The word always implies crossing a line from enough to too much.

examples.english: The reporters faced a hostile crowd outside the courthouse.
examples.persian: خبرنگاران بیرون از دادگاه با جمعیتی خصمانه روبرو شدند.

examples.english: The company attempted a hostile takeover of its smaller rival.
examples.persian: شرکت اقدام به یک تصاحب خصمانه رقیب کوچک‌ترش کرد.

examples.english: Few plants can survive in such a hostile desert climate.
examples.persian: تعداد کمی از گیاهان می‌توانند در چنین آب‌وهوای خصمانه و بیابانی زنده بمانند.

miniContext: Hostile describes open unfriendliness or opposition, whether between people, companies, or even environments. A hostile crowd outside a courthouse makes its anger visible, while a hostile takeover sees one company seize control of another against its wishes. The word also describes harsh natural conditions, as in a hostile desert climate where few plants survive. In every case, hostile signals active resistance rather than simple disagreement.

examples.english: The impatient driver honked repeatedly at the car ahead.
examples.persian: راننده بی‌صبر چندین بار برای ماشین جلویی بوق زد.

examples.english: Investors grew impatient waiting for the company to announce its quarterly results.
examples.persian: سرمایه‌گذاران از انتظار برای اعلام نتایج فصلی شرکت بی‌صبر شدند.

examples.english: Children in the long line became increasingly impatient as the show was delayed.
examples.persian: بچه‌ها در صف طولانی هر لحظه بی‌صبرتر می‌شدند چون نمایش به تأخیر افتاده بود.

miniContext: Impatient describes an inability to wait calmly, whether in traffic, in business, or in a long line. An impatient driver might honk repeatedly at the car ahead, while impatient investors grow frustrated waiting for a company's results. Children are often especially impatient, showing their restlessness openly when something is delayed. The word suggests a shortage of patience rather than a lack of interest.

examples.english: His impulsive decision to quit his job surprised everyone in the office.
examples.persian: تصمیم تکانشی او برای ترک کارش همه را در دفتر شگفت‌زده کرد.

examples.english: Teenagers are often more impulsive than adults because their brains are still developing.
examples.persian: نوجوانان معمولاً نسبت به بزرگسالان تکانشی‌تر هستند، چون مغزشان هنوز در حال رشد است.

examples.english: She regretted the impulsive purchase as soon as she got home.
examples.persian: به محض رسیدن به خانه، از خرید تکانشی‌اش پشیمان شد.

miniContext: Impulsive describes actions taken suddenly, without much thought about the consequences. An impulsive decision to quit a job can feel liberating in the moment but risky in hindsight. Psychologists note that teenagers tend to be more impulsive than adults because the brain's decision-making regions are still developing. The word often implies some regret follows, as when an impulsive purchase turns out to be unnecessary.

examples.english: He felt insecure about his English after moving to a new country.
examples.persian: او بعد از نقل‌مکان به کشور جدید، نسبت به زبان انگلیسی‌اش احساس عدم اعتمادبه‌نفس می‌کرد.

examples.english: Many new teachers feel insecure during their first weeks in the classroom.
examples.persian: بسیاری از معلمان تازه‌کار در هفته‌های اول در کلاس احساس ناامنی و بی‌اعتمادی به نفس می‌کنند.

examples.english: Constant criticism from her boss made her feel insecure about her abilities.
examples.persian: انتقاد مداوم رئیسش باعث شد او نسبت به توانایی‌هایش احساس بی‌اعتمادی به نفس کند.

miniContext: Insecure describes a lack of confidence, whether about a skill, a relationship, or one's place in a new environment. Someone who feels insecure about their English after moving abroad may hesitate to speak up in meetings. New teachers often feel insecure during their first weeks in the classroom, unsure whether students respect them. Constant criticism from others can deepen this feeling, making a person doubt abilities they actually have.

examples.english: The athletes trained under intense heat during the summer camp.
examples.persian: ورزشکاران در طول اردوی تابستانی زیر گرمای شدید تمرین کردند.

examples.english: Competition for the scholarship was intense this year, with over a thousand applicants.
examples.persian: امسال رقابت برای بورسیه بسیار شدید بود، با بیش از هزار متقاضی.

examples.english: She felt an intense wave of relief when she heard her son was safe.
examples.persian: او موج شدیدی از آرامش را حس کرد وقتی شنید پسرش سالم است.

miniContext: Intense describes anything unusually strong in degree, whether heat, emotion, or competition. Athletes training in intense summer heat must take extra precautions to avoid exhaustion. Competition for a limited number of scholarships can also become intense when thousands of students apply for only a few spots. The word applies equally to physical sensations and emotional experiences, always suggesting something pushed to a high level.

examples.english: Despite winning the award, she remained modest about her achievement.
examples.persian: او با وجود بردن جایزه، درباره موفقیتش متواضع باقی ماند.

examples.english: The scientist was famously modest, always crediting his students for the discovery.
examples.persian: این دانشمند به‌خاطر فروتنی‌اش معروف بود و همیشه کشف را به شاگردانش نسبت می‌داد.

examples.english: He gave a modest account of his role in the rescue, downplaying his own courage.
examples.persian: او توصیفی متواضعانه از نقش خود در عملیات نجات ارائه داد و شجاعت خودش را کم‌رنگ جلوه داد.

miniContext: Modest describes a person's tendency to downplay their own achievements or abilities rather than boast about them. Someone who wins an award but remains modest avoids claiming excessive credit, and a modest scientist might insist on crediting students or colleagues instead of taking sole praise. Even in recounting a personally heroic moment, a modest person tends to downplay their own courage. The word carries a clearly positive tone, prized as a sign of humility rather than weakness.

examples.english: The film received negative reviews from almost every major critic.
examples.persian: این فیلم از تقریباً تمام منتقدان مطرح نقدهای منفی گرفت.

examples.english: A negative attitude can spread quickly through a team under pressure.
examples.persian: یک نگرش منفی می‌تواند به سرعت در یک تیم تحت فشار پخش شود.

examples.english: The company's profits turned negative for the first time in a decade.
examples.persian: سود شرکت برای اولین بار در یک دهه منفی شد.

miniContext: Negative describes anything unfavorable, pessimistic, or below zero, depending on context. A film can receive negative reviews from critics, just as a company's profits can turn negative for the first time in years. A negative attitude, meanwhile, describes a mindset that expects the worst, which can spread quickly through a team under pressure. The opposite of negative, positive, implies optimism, benefit, or a number above zero.

examples.english: Despite the setback, she remained optimistic about the project's future.
examples.persian: با وجود این شکست، او همچنان نسبت به آینده پروژه خوش‌بین بود.

examples.english: Economists are cautiously optimistic that inflation will fall next year.
examples.persian: اقتصاددانان با احتیاط نسبت به کاهش تورم در سال آینده خوش‌بین هستند.

examples.english: The doctor gave an optimistic prognosis after reviewing the test results.
examples.persian: پزشک پس از بررسی نتایج آزمایش‌ها، پیش‌بینی خوش‌بینانه‌ای ارائه داد.

miniContext: Optimistic describes a hopeful outlook, even when the situation is uncertain or difficult. Economists can be cautiously optimistic about falling inflation without claiming the problem is fully solved. A doctor who gives an optimistic prognosis is offering hope based on medical evidence, not simply trying to comfort a patient. The word always implies a forward-looking belief that things will improve.

examples.english: He took a passive role in the negotiations, letting his lawyer do the talking.
examples.persian: او در مذاکرات نقشی منفعل داشت و اجازه داد وکیلش صحبت کند.

examples.english: Children exposed to passive smoke face a higher risk of respiratory illness.
examples.persian: کودکانی که در معرض دود سیگار منفعل قرار می‌گیرند، در معرض خطر بیشتری برای بیماری‌های تنفسی هستند.

examples.english: Writers are often advised to avoid the passive voice in favor of direct, active sentences.
examples.persian: به نویسندگان اغلب توصیه می‌شود از صدای منفعل اجتناب کنند و به جای آن جملات مستقیم و فعال بنویسند.

miniContext: Passive describes a lack of action or control, whether in grammar, health, or behavior. Writers are often told to avoid the passive voice because it hides who is actually performing an action. In health, passive smoke exposure affects people who never chose to smoke themselves. A person who takes a passive role in a negotiation lets others make the decisions instead of participating directly.

examples.english: The landlord agreed to a reasonable rent after some negotiation.
examples.persian: صاحب‌خانه پس از کمی مذاکره با اجاره‌ای معقول موافقت کرد.

examples.english: It seems reasonable to expect a reply within a week.
examples.persian: منطقی به نظر می‌رسد که انتظار پاسخ ظرف یک هفته داشته باشیم.

examples.english: She made a reasonable argument that convinced even her harshest critics.
examples.persian: او استدلال منطقی‌ای ارائه کرد که حتی سخت‌گیرترین منتقدانش را هم قانع کرد.

miniContext: Reasonable describes something fair, sensible, or logically justified, whether a price, a request, or an argument. A landlord who agrees to a reasonable rent after negotiation has settled on a fair figure for both sides. An argument is reasonable when it can convince even people who disagreed at first. The word suggests a balance between extremes, avoiding both excessive demands and excessive concessions.

examples.english: He is quite reserved at first, but opens up once he gets to know you.
examples.persian: او در ابتدا نسبتاً کم‌حرف و محتاط است، اما وقتی بیشتر با او آشنا شوید، راحت‌تر می‌شود.

examples.english: Her reserved manner at the meeting was mistaken for disinterest.
examples.persian: رفتار کم‌حرف و محتاط او در جلسه به اشتباه بی‌علاقگی تصور شد.

examples.english: Unlike his outgoing brother, he has always been reserved around strangers.
examples.persian: برخلاف برادر اجتماعی‌اش، او همیشه در برابر غریبه‌ها کم‌حرف و محتاط بوده است.

miniContext: Reserved describes a quiet, cautious personality that doesn't reveal much emotion or opinion right away. Someone who is reserved at first may open up considerably once they trust the people around them. In a meeting, a reserved manner can be mistaken for disinterest, even when the person is paying close attention. The word contrasts with outgoing, which describes someone eager to engage with others immediately.

examples.english: Scientists remained skeptical of the company's claims until independent tests confirmed them.
examples.persian: دانشمندان نسبت به ادعاهای شرکت شکاک باقی ماندند تا اینکه آزمایش‌های مستقل آن‌ها را تأیید کرد.

examples.english: Investors are skeptical about the startup's ability to turn a profit so quickly.
examples.persian: سرمایه‌گذاران نسبت به توانایی این استارتاپ برای سودآوری سریع شکاک هستند.

examples.english: She gave him a skeptical look when he explained why he was late again.
examples.persian: او وقتی توضیح داد چرا دوباره دیر کرده، نگاهی شکاکانه به او انداخت.

miniContext: Skeptical describes doubt that requires evidence before accepting a claim as true. Scientists remain skeptical of new findings until independent tests confirm the results, protecting the field from premature conclusions. Investors can be skeptical about a startup's promises, especially when profits seem unlikely so soon. A skeptical look or question signals that someone wants proof rather than simple assurance.
